newsitem.title: USA: May, June Brent deflate in late U.S. paper trading.
newsitem.headline: May, June Brent deflate in late U.S. paper trading.

text.p: North Sea Brent deflated in late U.S. paper trading on Monday, portending weakness in tomorrow's session, traders said.
A full boat of May Brent switched hands at $17.72 a barrel, down six cents from the settlement of the International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) in London.
Three partial June cargoes traded, twice at $17.93 and once at $17.95, down from the IPE close of $17.97.
May/June Brent traded at least once at minus 25 cents, down two cents from a trade earlier in the day.
June/July was talked at minus 14-11 cents, while July/August was around minus 12-10 cents.
